question.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(X<x)=P(Z<\frac{x-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =-3$ and $\sigma =1.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<-2.63) & =P(Z<\frac{-2.63-(-3)}{1}) \\  & =P(Z<0.37) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.37) \\  & =Φ(0.37)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14263116/assets/2c1ea2bcf22af9054c47ef2377fed27ff419fa14c211bc16e71d430845ec131a.png)

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.37)=0.6443.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(X<-2.63)=0.6443.
$$
